passages.text: No change of circumstances can repair a defect of character.
passages.note: Hoping a new situation will fix inner problems

passages.text: If I quake, what matters it what I quake at? Our proper vice takes form in one or another shape, according to the sex, age, or temperament of the person, and, if we are capable of fear, will readily find terrors. The covetousness or the malignity which saddens me when I ascribe it to society, is my own. I am always environed by myself.
passages.note: Anxiety and fear that find new objects; looking inward
